subject: Audit log continuity & egress packaging — RFP follow-up
messages:
From: Hannah Lowe <legalops@emeraldbank.com>
To: kimberly.park@redwood.ai
Cc: simon.wu@emeraldbank.com
Date: Fri, 02 Apr 2027 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: RFP questions — audit log continuity, export packaging and proofs

Kimberly,

Thanks for the quick initial submission to our RFP. The legal and security teams had a few follow-ups specifically around long-term audit continuity and the mechanics of exporting audit data for regulatory review. Can you confirm the following at a high level and, if possible, provide an example manifest or brief sample output?

1) Export packaging: when we request a bulk export for a date range, what container formats do you provide (ndjson, parquet, gzipped tar)? Do you include a manifest with checksums for every file?
2) Chain-of-custody and tamper evidence: do exported objects include signed checksums or WORM indicators? How is tamper evidence demonstrated?
3) Metadata exposure: which fields are present per audit row by default (request_id, user_id, session_id, client_ip, model_version, token_count)? Can we request expanded fields for compliance?
4) Retention and purging: confirm retention enforcement (time-based, legal hold overrides), and whether deletions are soft or hard.
5) Transfer modes: S3 presigned, SFTP, encrypted physical media — which are supported; any lead times?

We are trying to lock these answers into the procurement schedule this week. If you have a short manifest sample and a recommended export timeline (hours/days), that would help.

Best,
Hannah Lowe
Senior Counsel, Legal Ops
Emerald Bank

—
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Lowe <legalops@emeraldbank.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 02 Apr 2027 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: RFP questions — audit log continuity, export packaging and proofs

Hannah —

Appreciate the detailed questions. Quick acknowledgement: we can provide all of the items you listed; below is a concise summary and I attached a short export spec + a sample evidence manifest for your team to review. If you want, we can run a small canary export for a non-production tenant this week.

Summary (high level):
- Container formats: ndjson (line-delimited JSON) or Parquet, compressed with gzip. Exports delivered as a versioned tarball (.tar.gz) with a manifest.csv listing files, row counts, and SHA256 checksums.
- Manifest and checksums: yes — every object has a SHA256 checksum recorded in the manifest. We can also provide a detached PGP signature for the manifest on request.
- Tamper evidence: manifests include generation timestamps and file checksums; we can sign manifests with an HSM-backed key and include signature metadata. For contractual WORM, we provide a timestamped, signed manifest and a tamper log showing any post-generation access attempts.
- Metadata fields: default audit rows include timestamp, request_id, route, user_id (pseudonymization available), session_id, client_ip (redactable), model_version, token_count, latency_ms, and event_type. Expanded fields (raw headers, full prompt) can be included under separate export scopes.
- Retention/purge: retention enforcement is time-based at the tenant level; deletions are hard after retention expiry unless a legal hold is applied. Legal holds override automatic purge and we provide hold release workflows.
- Transfer modes: preferred is S3 presigned PUT (recommended for large exports), SFTP over FTPS, or encrypted .tar.gz delivery via customer-provided S3 or Azure Blob. Physical media is supported for very large datasets with an additional security review and 5–10 business-day lead time.

Attachments: Redwood_Audit_Export_Spec_v1.2.pdf, evidence_manifest_sample.csv

Next steps — if youd like a canary export: propose we schedule a 2-hr window next business day; we’ll provision a dedicated export job and provide a presigned S3 URL and manifest.

Kimberly Park
Head of Product Compliance
Redwood Inference

From: Simon Wu <simon.wu@emeraldbank.com>
To: kimberly.park@redwood.ai
Cc: legalops@emeraldbank.com
Date: Sat, 03 Apr 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: RFP questions — audit log continuity, export packaging and proofs

Kimberly —

Thanks for the quick reply and the attachments. Couple of clarifying items from Infra/Security:

- For manifests signed with an HSM key: can you provide details on your key rotation policy and whether we can verify signatures against a published public key?
- For record-level pseudonymization: what fields are pseudonymized (user_id only, or session_id/request_id too)? Is the mapping reversible by a customer under key control?
- For retention enforcement: do you offer an immutable backup snapshot for a given tenant as a separate retention tier (i.e., an isolated archive that cannot be auto-purged without a manual process)?
- For transfers: is there an option to get exports already partitioned by day (YYYY/MM/DD) inside the tarball to ease incremental ingestion?

Also, what is your SLA for producing a standard 90-day export (50GB compressed) and for a full-year export (2TB compressed)? We need an estimate for procurement.

Simon Wu
Director, Infrastructure Security
Emerald Bank

—
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Simon Wu <simon.wu@emeraldbank.com>, Hannah Lowe <legalops@emeraldbank.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 04 Apr 2027 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: RFP questions — audit log continuity, export packaging and proofs

Simon/Hannah —

Detailed answers below; I kept each item short and flagged where we can provide an artifact or an example flow. Happy to set up a technical runbook walkthrough with Marissa (Customer Success) and Ben (Security) if you want deeper ops-level detail.

1) HSM signature / key rotation:
- We sign manifests with an HSM-backed RSA 4096 key stored in a KMS (AWS KMS or customer-managed HSM for Private deployments). Rotation cadence is quarterly or upon incident; rotated keys are kept in a key-history register and old public keys remain available for signature verification for 18 months. We publish a key metadata file and an X.509 certificate chain you can validate. Artifact: sample-signed-manifest.asc (available on request).

2) Pseudonymization and reversibility:
- Default pseudonymization: user_id is pseudonymized (one-way salted hash) by default; request_id and session_id remain deterministic identifiers (not reversible) to allow cross-record joins.
- Customer reversible mapping: for customers on Private or Dedicated plans we can support reversible pseudonymization under a customer-controlled key (requires HSM integration and configuration during onboarding).

3) Immutable archive tier:
- Yes. We offer an isolated immutable archive option (immutable S3 bucket with object lock Governance mode) for customers who require a separate retention tier. That archive is created on-demand and locked for the requested retention window; we log the archive creation and include it in the manifest.

4) Partitioning and packaging:
- Exports can be partitioned daily (YYYY/MM/DD) inside the tarball by date-range scope. We recommend daily partitions for large ranges to speed incremental ingestion.

5) SLA / throughput estimates (guideline):
- 90-day export (~50GB compressed): typical turnaround 6–12 hours for scheduled exports; we aim for same-business-day delivery for HSM-signed manifests.
- 1-year export (~2TB compressed): typical turnaround 2–5 business days depending on queueing and whether physical transfer is requested.
- For time-sensitive legal requests, we offer an expedited pipeline (SLA add-on) with a guaranteed 24–48 hour window for exports up to 1TB.

Operational notes:
- Checksums: SHA256 for every object in manifest.csv; manifest includes row counts, first/last timestamps per file, and generation node id.
- Chain-of-custody: when we run an export, we log the job id and the operator (automated service principal or human) and persist an export audit record in an append-only ledger for 18 months.
- Transfer modes: S3 presigned (recommended), SFTP, or direct delivery to a customer bucket. Physical media requires coordination and an additional security review.

Attachments referenced above: the export spec contains a sample manifest and a small CSV stub (evidence_manifest_sample.csv) illustrating the checksum columns and file layout.

Can we schedule a 30-minute technical sync on Monday to walk through the canary export flow? Marissa — can you propose two 30-min windows? Ben — I included you in case we need to pull a runbook.

Thanks,
Kimberly
